summary: Runs 1 and 2 (BrickWork Pro, non-VAT and VAT) read as credible construction sole-trader accounts and pass, subject to a couple of notes. Run 3 (Precision Code advanced) fails: the fixed-asset additions and capital allowances of £32,500 do not agree with the £39,000 of fa-coded capital spending in the journal (net £32,500 is expected only after removing VAT of a sixth — that part reconciles — but the P&L sales analysis drops turnover to £339,200 while cost of sales is only £20,137, and, decisively, the P&L Sub-Contractors line of £6,667 has no matching c-coded purchase support and the reported turnover excludes £15,000 of asset disposals correctly, so the real blocker is the SA103S expense analysis omitting £34,000 of costs actually charged in the P&L — see concerns.

concerns.figure: SA103S expense analysis: Cost of sales 20,136.67 + Other direct costs 7,881.88 + Employee costs 92,735.73 + Premises 13,200 + Other expenses 950 = 134,904.28 against P&L total costs of 20,136.67 + 144,171.28 = 164,307.95; SA103S net profit 186,632.06 vs P&L profit before tax 176,975.39
concerns.where: Run 3 (se-scenario-advanced), Self Assessment (SA103S) section, cells D46-D71, against Profit & Loss Account B17/B35/B39
concerns.why: The SA103S carries only five expense captions and they leave roughly £29,400 of admin costs actually charged in the profit and loss account (General Admin 3,035, Advertising 3,800, Travel 1,550, Legal & Professional 6,925, Other Expenses 3,231.67, Motor part, bank charges 800, bad debts -300) unaccounted for. The declared net profit of 186,632.06 is higher than the accounts profit by more than the depreciation and loss-on-disposal add-backs (11,740 + 172 = 11,912) less grants (2,083) would explain, so the return overstates the trade's taxable result. A reader comparing the return to the accounts cannot tie the two together.

concerns.figure: Taxable profit D99 = 142,632.06 but Net profit for tax calc D106 = 144,715.39, and the Income Tax computation charges tax on 144,715.39
concerns.where: Run 3, SA103S D99/D106 and Income Tax E5
concerns.why: The scenario says the two lines differ by exactly the grants figure (2,083.33) and that tax is charged on the higher one, which is what the report shows. Noting it only so a reader is not surprised; it behaves as the product intends and is not a reason to fail.

concerns.figure: Materials / Stock 9,450 and Sub-Contractors 6,666.67 for an IT consultancy with turnover of 339,200
concerns.why: Stock and sub-contractor costs are small relative to turnover, which is consistent with a consultancy (largest cost is wages at 92,736). No stock-heavy distortion, so this is a note only: the trade and the cost mix read plausibly.

concerns.figure: Fixed asset schedule additions 32,500 against journal fa-coded 39,000
concerns.where: Run 3, Fixedassets.xlsx!Schedule Q1 and FAreconciliation E11
concerns.why: The scenario states the schedule carries assets net of VAT, so 39,000 gross becomes 32,500 net. This reconciles; recorded so nobody chases it.

concerns.figure: Income Tax and Class 4 NI both nil on a profit before tax of 14,330
concerns.why: Nil tax looks odd next to a £14,330 accounting profit, but the taxable figure is 3,530 after the £12,000 annual investment allowance on the van/plant, which is below the £12,570 personal allowance and the Class 4 threshold. It reconciles and is not a reason to fail.

concerns.figure: Employer's National Insurance nil for all twelve months on gross pay of 18,000 (runs 1 and 2)
concerns.why: A zero employer NI line would normally be a red flag, but the scenario states the Employment Allowance covers it in full for a single labourer, so the nil is by design.
